rationale: The paid market is real — Paragon and Tuxera charge $20–40 one-time fees and people pay — so willingness_to_pay is strong and the buyer (prosumers, small studio staff swapping external drives) is identifiable. However, the opportunity itself is a kernel-level NTFS driver, which the original poster correctly notes requires low-level OS hooks and bypasses OS protections: this is not buildable with Claude prompts, a landing page, and Stripe. A cloud sync bridge workaround exists conceptually but is a fundamentally different product competing with Dropbox and is not the stated pain. Buildability_with_ai scores 2 and operational_autonomy scores 3 because driver delivery, installation support, and OS-compatibility edge cases require substantial engineering and human-in-the-loop support — not a factory play.
solution_plan: This is not a viable build for this factory. The core product is a macOS kernel-space filesystem driver requiring deep systems programming well beyond Claude prompts and standard tooling. A workaround product (e.g., a cloud-sync bridge) sidesteps the actual pain and enters a crowded market without differentiation. A solo non-technical operator cannot realistically build, ship, or support a driver product here. Drop and move on.
notes: buildability_with_ai fails gate (score 2, min 6); operational_autonomy fails gate (score 3, min 7). Total also below min_total_to_validate (4.9 < 5.5).
